title: BLAKE3 1-block 7-round compression kernel (64 bytes)

target_block_header.x86_64: for x86_64 needs avx needs avx512 { ... }

contract_header:
use spec = "2obgvxo5y6cn27cz7gn4mxieudnb4chhosahlutaeauwmgfhzqwq"  // blake3_compress1_spec.ode

fn blake3_compress1(h: 32 bytes, m: 64 bytes, length: word, t: counter, flags: low word)
    requires no_overlap(h, m)
    ensures h = bytes_of(spec.compress(words(h), words(m), t, length, flags))
    stack 256
task_summary: Implement `blake3_compress1(h, m, length, t, flags)`, the official BLAKE3 7-round single-block compression function (BLAKE3 paper section 2.2): given an 8-word chaining value `h` (`32 bytes`), a 16-word message block `m` (`64 bytes`), `length: word`, 64-bit counter `t: counter`, and `flags: low word`, run 7 rounds with the BLAKE3 message permutation between rounds and write `[s[7][i] ^ s[7][i + 8] for i in 0..8]` back to `h[0..32]` in place. Use `u32x4` SIMD vector operations (plus `std/vec.ode`'s `vec.rotr32`, `vec.pack_u64x2`, `vec.const_u32x4`, or `data ...` + `const_u32x4(...)` on x86-64, together with `uzp1_32`, `uzp2_32`, `shuf32`, `shufps`, `blend32`, `unpacklo32`, `unpackhi32`, `unpacklo64`, `ext4`, `ext8`, `ext12`) and hygienic `inline fn (var ...)` helpers. Your goal is BOTH full verification (`shown`) AND minimum cycles per 64-byte block.
opt_goal: reduce total cycles per 64-byte compression (and `cyc/B`) by minimizing message-permutation shuffles, hiding rotate/add latency, and keeping zero stack spills while preserving `shown` verification and native tests
